Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

human adjective and noun

also human being, humans, the human race, humankind, mankind, man, humane

classical

Ter. Heaut. 77: hūmānī nihil ā mē aliēnum putō
Liv. 21.30.7: hūmānō generī
Plin. NH 8.1: proximumque hūmānīs sēnsibus
Traupman 330

hūmānus, hūmāna, hūmānum

declension

human, of people

The human race is genus hūmānum (Cic. Amic. 20, Lewis & Short). Of a person, hūmānus also means “kind, civilised, cultivated” (hūmānitās).

Other words

  • homō, hominis m. — a human being

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 77: Homō sum; Traupman 330: human being, homō; Traupman 330

  • mortālis, mortālis m. — a mortal, a human (as against the gods)

    noun (the adjective mortālis used as a noun), declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.327–328: haud tibi vultus mortālis

Examples

  • Homō sum: hūmānī nihil ā mē aliēnum putō.

    I am human: I count nothing human foreign to me.Ter. Heaut. 77

  • nūllās profectō terrās caelum contingere nec inexsuperābilēs hūmānō generī esse

    no land actually touches the sky, and none is beyond the human race to crossLiv. 21.30.7

  • maximum est elephāns proximumque hūmānīs sēnsibus

    the largest is the elephant, and the nearest to human feelingPlin. NH 8.1

See also people, individual.

SourcesLewis & Short: humanus · Lewis & Short: homo · Lewis & Short: mortalis
